you: stretch a rope between two drifting anchors and play it like a slingshot
sing notes whose loudness physically shoves everything nearby
fold the level like paper along lines you draw with your finger
swap bodies with whatever you point at for as long as you hold your breath
freeze one object in time at a time; freezing a second thaws the first
dig tunnels that only your followers can see or use
pour paint; each color changes the physics of whatever it soaks
throw your shadow ahead of you and then become it
stack tiny planets and let their combined gravity do the rest
tune a radio dial where every frequency rewrites one rule of the room
draw a loop on the ground; everything inside replays its last five seconds
grow vines from your fingertips toward whichever light you carry
whistle to call echoes that copy your last move a beat later
pinch the camera to shrink or enlarge the room while you stay the same size
hand every creature a single instruction card that it obeys far too literally
lend your weight to a scale that balances two separate worlds
mark things with chalk; whatever is chalked breaks next
rotate the entire level a quarter turn while gravity stays exactly where it is
carry the only lantern; nothing exists outside its glow
juggle three timers; each one runs a different law of the room
tie knots in the path behind you so pursuers tangle in them
pluck strings between walls to launch yourself like an arrow
spend memories to buy skills; you can hold only three at once
conduct a crowd of tiny followers with the tempo of a baton
write one word on a wall and the wall starts behaving like that word
pour yourself into containers and flow through the level as liquid, gas or ice
trade places with your own reflection in any mirror, window or puddle
wear a single magnet and flip its polarity to push or pull the world
lay down track one piece at a time while a runaway cart gains on you
cut the level along any straight line and slide the two halves apart
plant seeds that grow into whatever object you were holding when you planted them
keep a pet storm on a leash and aim its lightning with your footsteps
but: every object you touch gets a little heavier for the rest of the level
the left half of the world runs at half speed
a ghost repeats everything you do exactly one beat late
walls are solid only while you are looking at them
you can never touch the same surface twice in a row
gravity points toward the last thing you touched
the level shrinks every time you succeed
tools never break; they wear down into different tools
everything mirrors itself the moment you stand still
silence is solid and noise is a doorway
numbers painted on things are real; a 7 weighs seven times a 1
the floor gives way on your third visit to any tile
you can only move while a partner you do not control moves
your color is a rule; only matching things help or hurt you; it changes with each item you carry
time passes only when you change direction
thrown objects remember where they came from and return when thrown again
light bends around the biggest thing on screen
the exit drifts toward whatever you ignore the longest
every move costs a coin and you earn coins only by standing still
a bell rings every ten seconds and you must pick one of three new laws
friend and foe swap sides whenever you cross the midline
the more you carry the smaller you become
shadows are separate objects that can be picked up
speed is shared; whatever you speed up slows something else down
you may only ever turn left
anything you stop looking at falls asleep and stays that way
each new room is built from your last three mistakes
your inventory is physical and trails behind you like a tail
up is whichever way you last fell
everything you create vanishes the moment you create something new

pushback: A slow tide of ink rises from below and erases whatever it touches.
A rival copy of you plays the same level one step ahead and spoils your route.
The level crumbles from the edges toward the center on a visible countdown.
A hungry crowd follows you and eats anything you leave unattended.
A storm front sweeps across the map and scatters your tools if it catches them.
Every ten seconds the room swaps its rules with the room next door.
A quiet creature mirrors your mistakes back at you with interest.
Your energy drains faster the more you succeed.
A wall closes in from one side; each push back costs something you cannot get again.
Echoes of your earlier attempts haunt the level and block your old routes.
Gravity grows stronger with every item you collect.
A flock of thieves steals whatever you set down.
A clock-faced beast eats a minute of your day each time it catches you.
The map builds itself one screen ahead of you while one screen behind decays.
Noise draws a patient listener that always arrives from a new direction.
An unseen second player is solving the same puzzle and moves things behind your back.
Every success wakes something bigger.
Fog rolls in and everything you have not touched recently is forgotten.
A pendulum of light sweeps the level and scorches anything standing still.
Your tools multiply when unused and swarm you if you hoard them.
The ground is a slow conveyor and the whole level drifts to the left.
You carry a fragile guest who panics at sudden moves.
A debt grows every second; only risky moves pay it down.
A tide of rival ghosts races you to claim the same objects.
goal: Reach the exit still holding something you started with.
Light every lamp without ever lighting two in neighboring rooms.
Return a lost creature to the place where it first appeared.
Build one unbroken chain from one end of the world to the other.
Empty the level until nothing is left but you.
Balance everything: finish with exactly the same amount on both sides.
Survive until the final bell while doing as little as possible.
Gather five parts of a machine and assemble them in the right order.
Teach a stubborn crowd one dance step.
Escape through a door that exists only once you stop searching for it.
Reach the highest point without ever going down.
Draw a picture with your path that a stranger would recognize.
Put every enemy to sleep at the same moment.
Carry a sleeping friend through ten rooms without waking them.
Give each of your tools to the right person before the level ends.
Grow one thing to full size before anything else around it can.
Leave the level exactly as you found it.
Reach a stranger on the far side who has the very same problem.
Finish with the fewest actions; the quietest run scores highest.
Win a round by deliberately losing the round before it.
Fill the whole map with color.
Teach your pursuer to stop chasing.
Make the loudest sound the level is able to make.
Be the last thing standing in a world that shrinks to a point.
story: A retired lighthouse keeper in a harbor town that is slowly floating away.
A courier in a city whose streets rearrange themselves every night.
The last apprentice of a clockmaker who stopped time and then vanished.
A stray cat that the whole neighborhood believes is a small god.
A cartographer mapping a country that dislikes being mapped.
A night nurse at a hospital that treats broken machines.
A kite maker whose kites carry messages between rival mountains.
A ghost who must finish one chore before the house can be sold.
A deep sea diver who keeps finding rooms that were built for her.
A baker whose bread remembers whoever eats it.
A traveling choir with one voice missing and a long road ahead.
A robot gardener tending a park for people who have all left.
A student whose homework turns into the place they must walk through.
A pair of twins who share one pair of hands.
A beekeeper on a space station with no flowers.
A forgotten statue that gets exactly one night each year to move.
A sailor on a ship that sails across the sky at low tide.
A mail carrier delivering letters addressed to people who do not exist yet.
A tiny dragon applying for a very ordinary job.
A librarian guarding a book that rewrites whoever reads it.
A thief who must return everything they ever stole, one night at a time.
A lamplighter in a town where the dark is alive and rather shy.
A grandmother driving a very slow, very important truck.
A tour guide leading visitors through a city that exists only while it is being described.
